transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi. I came in because... well, my brain just feels like it stalls out. I'll be at work, sitting with a test report or even just a simple CAD note open on my screen for an hour, and I just can't decide what the next sentence should be. Or even what checkbox to click. I just get completely stuck.
Over the past couple of weeks, how has your overall mood been? Would you say you've been feeling down, sad, or depressed?

I'm not entirely sure. I guess I've been feeling down, maybe? But I haven't really noticed feeling sad in the usual way... it's mostly just that stalled feeling I mentioned. I just feel kind of blank.
When did you first notice this stalled feeling and difficulty concentrating? Was it gradual over weeks, or did it come on more suddenly?

I think it started... well, it's been going on since I got moved into the prototype-testing role at work. That was about a year and a month ago. It wasn't just overnight, but looking back, that's definitely when I first started noticing that I couldn't seem to get my brain to move forward on things.

When you feel stuck like this, do you notice any physical symptoms in your body — like your heart racing, sweating, muscle tension, or a feeling of panic — or is it mainly just the mental difficulty with deciding and moving forward?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My heart doesn't race, and I don't feel panicky or tense. It's really just... the mental part. I just sit there looking at the screen, and my brain just won't go to the next step.
Over this past year, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels?

I don't really think so. My sleep has been pretty much the same as it always is, and I'm still eating normally. As for energy... I mean, I have that blank feeling I told you about, but I wouldn't say I feel physically tired or wiped out. So, no, I haven't really noticed any changes with those things.
Are there activities or hobbies that you normally enjoy — things you'd usually look forward to doing — and have you noticed yourself losing interest in those things over this past year?

Yeah, I have. I used to really like 3D printing miniatures, but... my printer has just been sitting there with the same half-finished figure on it for months now. I just haven't had any desire to touch it. And even things like yoga, or just going for a walk in the woods, which I used to enjoy... they just feel like chores now. It feels like just another task I have to get through, instead of something I actually want to do.

Over this past year, on most days when you wake up, would you say you feel a persistent low mood or sadness throughout the day, or is the blank, stuck feeling more of a mental fog that comes and goes?

I wouldn't say I feel sad, really. It's not a low mood like... crying or feeling down. It's just that blankness. And it doesn't really come and go, it's just kind of always there. I wake up and I just feel... empty, I guess. Like there's just nothing there most days.
Over this past year, have you found yourself feeling guilty, worthless, or blaming yourself for things? Or do you feel like you're a burden to others?

Yeah, I do feel that way. I'll catch myself... I just keep replaying these really tiny mistakes from the lab. And instead of just moving on from them, I end up telling myself that I'm not just bad at this job, but that I'm actually a bad person. It feels like I deserve whatever consequences come from those mistakes. So, yeah, I guess I do blame myself and feel pretty worthless a lot of the time.
Over this past year, have you ever had thoughts about harming yourself or wished that you were dead?

Yeah, I have. Mostly when I'm driving. On my commute, I'll catch myself thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't arrive anywhere. And sometimes... the idea of just steering off the road pops into my head, and it actually scares me enough that I have to grip the steering wheel and pull over for a minute.

Have you ever had a period of time, lasting at least a few days, where you felt unusually energetic, optimistic, or like your thoughts were racing ahead of you — maybe taking on lots of projects or needing less sleep than usual?

No, I haven't ever felt like that. I don't really get bursts of energy or feel overly optimistic. And I definitely don't have times where I need less sleep or want to take on a bunch of projects. It's really just been that constant blank, empty feeling I mentioned before.

Symptoms have been present for approximately 13 months since a work role change, meeting duration criteria for major depressive disorder. Absence of manic/hypomanic episodes, panic symptoms, or significant neurovegetative changes (sleep, appetite, energy remain unchanged). The cognitive difficulties (decision-making paralysis, concentration) are consistent with depressive cognition rather than primary attention deficit. F32.9 (Major Depressive Disorder, single episode, unspecified severity) is the most appropriate diagnosis.
